items.prompt: What is the name of the planet we live on?

figure.alt: Our planet, round with blue seas and green and brown land.

options.why: The Moon goes around our planet. We do not live on it.
The Sun is a star. We live on a planet.

hints: Think about the planet under your feet.
It has land, seas and lots of living things.
The name is also a word for soil.
items.explanation: We live on planet Earth. It has land, water and lots of living things.

items.prompt: What does the Sun give us?

options.why: Rain falls from clouds.
The Sun makes the day bright.

hints: How does the Sun make you feel when you stand in it?
items.explanation: The Sun gives us light and heat. It makes the day bright and warms the land and the sea.

items.prompt: The Sun is a huge ball of very hot gas. It is a ___.
hints: At night we see many tiny ones twinkling.
The Sun is one of these, but it is much closer to us.
It is a 4-letter word and also a shape with points.
items.explanation: The Sun is a star. It looks bigger and brighter than other stars because it is much closer to Earth.

items.prompt: Choose all the things we can find on the Earth's land.

options.why: The Sun is far away in space.
Stars are far away in space.

hints: Think about what you see when you travel.
Ask: could I stand on it or next to it?
Start with the mountains. Are they on the land?
items.explanation: Mountains, rivers and rocks are on the Earth's land. The Sun and the stars are far away in space.

items.prompt: Why must you never look straight at the Sun?

options.why: The danger is to your eyes. The Sun is too bright.
The Sun stays in the sky when you look at it.

hints: The Sun is very, very bright.
Which body part do you use to look?
Think about why people wear sun hats and sunglasses outside.
items.explanation: The Sun is so bright that looking straight at it can hurt your eyes. Never look at it, even with sunglasses on.
items.tip: Never look straight at the Sun.

items.prompt: What covers most of the Earth?

figure.alt: The Earth from space, mostly blue sea with some green and brown land.

options.why: There are sandy deserts, but much more of the Earth is sea.
Some places are icy, but much more of the Earth is sea.

hints: Look at a globe. What colour is most of it?
Ask: what do the blue parts on a map stand for?
Compare the blue parts with the green and brown parts.
items.explanation: Most of the Earth is covered by water in seas and oceans. That is why the Earth looks blue from space.

items.prompt: Is it on Earth or in space? Sort the cards.

figure.alt: Six pictures: the sea, a volcano, a forest, the Sun, the Moon and stars.

hints: Space is far above the sky.
Ask: could I walk or swim there?
Start with the sea. Can you swim in it?
items.explanation: The sea, volcanoes and forests are on Earth. The Sun, the Moon and the stars are in space.

items.prompt: What shape is the Earth?

options.why: Photos taken from space show that the Earth is round.
The Earth has no corners.

hints: Think about the globe in your classroom.
Photos taken from space show its shape.
Picture the Earth from a rocket.
items.explanation: The Earth is round like a ball. Photos from space show its round shape.

items.prompt: Citra hangs wet clothes outside on a sunny day. Why do they dry?

figure.alt: Wet clothes hanging outside in the sunshine.

options.why: The Moon does not give out heat.
Cold makes wet things dry more slowly.

hints: Think about what the Sun gives us.
Do clothes dry faster on hot days or cold days?
Picture clothes on a line at midday.
items.explanation: The Sun's heat warms the wet clothes, and the water dries up into the air.

items.prompt: The Sun is huge, but it looks small in the sky. Why?

options.text: It is smaller than a car.
options.why: The Sun is much bigger than the whole Earth.
Even on a clear day it looks small because it is so far away.

hints: Think about how a plane looks high in the sky.
Things look smaller when they are far away.
Compare a bus near you with a bus far down the road.
items.explanation: The Sun is huge, much bigger than the Earth. It looks small because it is very, very far away.

items.prompt: Why is the Sun important for living things?

options.why: Night is dark because the Sun's light is not reaching us.

options.text: It gives us water to drink.
options.why: Our water comes from rain, rivers and wells.

hints: Think about what plants and animals need.
What does the Sun give to the Earth?
Picture a plant growing in a sunny garden.
items.explanation: The Sun gives light and warmth. Plants need light to grow, and animals need plants for food.

items.prompt: The Sun is a star. Why does it look brighter than other stars?

figure.alt: The bright Sun and some small, faint stars.

options.why: Other stars are huge too. They are much further away.

options.text: It is much closer to Earth than other stars.

options.why: All stars are very hot balls of gas.

hints: Remember what happens to things that are far away.
Other stars are suns too, but where are they?
Compare how far away the Sun is with the night stars.
items.explanation: The Sun is the closest star to Earth. Other stars are so far away that they look like tiny dots of light.

items.prompt: When can we see the Sun in the sky?

options.why: At night it is dark.
We see the Sun on dry days too.

hints: Think about when it is light.
items.explanation: We see the Sun in the daytime.

items.prompt: What can we see in the sky at night?

options.why: The Sun is shining on the other side of the Earth.
A rainbow needs sunlight.

items.explanation: At night we can see the Moon and the stars if the sky is clear.

items.prompt: Why is it warm on a sunny day?

options.why: The Moon does not make heat.
Clouds do not make heat.

hints: It is in the sky in the day.
items.explanation: The Sun gives us light and heat.

items.prompt: What do plants need from the Sun?

options.why: Plants do not need sound.
Plants do not need toys.

hints: Plants grow on a bright window.
items.explanation: Plants need sunlight to grow well.

items.prompt: How can you stay safe on a very sunny day?

options.text: wear a hat and sit in the shade

options.why: This hurts your eyes.

options.text: stay in the Sun all day
options.why: You can get burned.

hints: The Sun can hurt your eyes.
items.explanation: A hat and some shade keep us safe from the strong Sun.

items.prompt: Which is the biggest?

figure.alt: The Sun, the Earth and the Moon.

options.why: The Sun is much bigger.
The Moon is smallest.

items.explanation: The Sun is much bigger than the Earth and the Moon.

items.prompt: What is the Moon?

options.why: The Moon is not a star.
The Moon goes around the Earth, so it is not a planet.

items.explanation: The Moon is a big ball of rock. It goes around the Earth.

items.prompt: Day or night? Sort the cards.
hints: The Sun shines in the day.
Stars are seen in the dark.
items.explanation: The Sun, a blue sky and a rainbow are seen in the day. The Moon and stars are seen at night.

items.prompt: Does it make its own light? Sort the cards.
hints: A torch makes its own light.
A mirror needs light to shine.
items.explanation: The Sun, a torch and a candle make light. The Moon, a mirror and a book only reflect light.

items.prompt: Choose all the plants that need sunlight.
items.explanation: A sunflower, a tree and grass are plants. Plants need sunlight to grow.

items.prompt: Put the parts of a day in order. Start with the morning.
items.explanation: A day starts in the morning. Then comes the afternoon, the evening and the night.

items.prompt: The ___ is in the sky in the day. The ___ and stars are in the sky at night.
items.explanation: The Sun is in the sky in the day. The Moon and stars are in the sky at night.

items.prompt: What do we see in the sky?
head: Time
We see
hints: The Moon comes out at night.
items.explanation: We see the Sun in the day and the Moon at night.

items.prompt: Putri plays outside in the morning. The Sun is bright and warm. In the evening the Sun goes down. Now the sky is dark and she sees the Moon and stars.

parts.prompt: What does Putri see at night?

items.explanation: The sky is dark at night. Putri sees the Moon and stars.

items.prompt: Tap the Sun.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: Sun, Moon, cloud and rainbow.

items.explanation: The Sun is the bright star that gives us light and heat.

items.prompt: Tap what we see in the sky at night.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: Sun, Moon, rainbow and umbrella.

items.explanation: We can see the Moon in the night sky.

items.prompt: Draw the sky in the day and the sky at night.

criteria.label: Draws the Sun in the day sky
Draws the Moon or stars in the night sky

hints: Add the Sun to the day sky.
items.explanation: The day sky is light with the Sun. The night sky is dark with the Moon and stars.

items.prompt: Which cannot happen at night?

options.why: This can happen at night.
This can happen at night.
This can happen at night.

hints: Moon and stars are for the night.
items.explanation: The Sun is not in our sky at night, so it cannot make shadows. We can see the Moon and stars and hear owls.

items.prompt: One ice cube is in the shade. One is in the Sun. Which melts first?

options.why: The shade is cooler.

options.text: they melt at the same time
options.why: The Sun is hotter.

items.explanation: The Sun gives heat, so the ice cube in the Sun melts first.

items.prompt: At noon, which is the hottest to touch?

options.text: a metal slide in the shade
options.why: It is cooler out of the Sun.

options.text: a metal slide in the Sun
a wooden bench in the shade
options.why: It is cooler out of the Sun.
Ice is cold.

items.explanation: The Sun heats the metal slide a lot. Shade and ice stay cooler.
